intent: Inline status banner that stays on the page.
useWhen: Page or form feedback the user should still see after it appears
Success, warning, or danger copy tied to the current view
doNotUseWhen: Transient confirmations that disappear — not a toast; ask before adding one
A dismissible insight tile — use InsightCard

children.note: Optional: leave it out when the title says it all, like an error summary.

placement.note: page: tinted fill, for a problem that affects the whole page or account; put it above the content it is about. inline: neutral card surface with the status shown by the icon, for something in one part of the page. The header (tone word, eyebrow, timestamp, Dismiss) always shows on inline; on page it shows when eyebrow, timestamp or onDismiss is set.

eyebrow.note: Short context word after the tone word in the header, like Billing in Warning · Billing.

timestamp.note: Preformatted time on the right of the header, like Nov 20 or 09:41.

action.note: One kit Button under the text. page: solid primary (counts as the view's one primary), or outline neutral with appearance "outline" when the page already has its primary (an error summary above a form with Save). inline: outline neutral.

appearance.note: action only; page placement only. inline is always outline.

icon.note: Leading Lucide icon on the Button, aria-hidden, such as RotateCcw on Retry. The label still names the action.

secondaryAction.note: kit Button outline neutral, after action.

onDismiss.note: () => void. Shows a Dismiss kit Button on the right of the header. Leave it out while the problem is still real.

requirements: info, success and warning use role=status (a warning on page load is not urgent)
The header starts with the tone word (Info, Success, Warning, Error from KitLabelsProvider keys info, success, warning, danger), then · eyebrow, so status is never colour alone
Title uses the -fg tone and body uses text.primary (4.5:1 or more on the tinted fill); the icon keeps the status colour
Dismiss is a kit Button named Dismiss (KitLabelsProvider); focus never jumps to the alert
Actions are kit Buttons, so they stay keyboard reachable in reading order after the text
An action icon (action.icon, secondaryAction.icon) is decorative and aria-hidden; the label still names the action, so never pass an icon without a label

doNot: Do not invent local Alert, Banner, or Callout
Do not use Alert for toast-style popups
Do not pass actions as ReactNode slots — use action and secondaryAction
Do not use more than two actions in one Alert
snippet:
<Alert variant="warning" placement="inline" eyebrow="Billing" timestamp="Nov 20" title="Card expires on Dec 12" action={{ label: "Update card", onClick: openBilling }} onDismiss={hide}>
  Update the card before then or the workspace pauses.
</Alert>
